verdict.identity_confidence: high at the generalized feature scale
verdict.summary: The complete supplied Natural Earth feature and decoded baseline represent the generalized principal body of Kamianske Reservoir. Official chart 3031 and an independent operator original support the reservoir identity, with both neighboring cascade reservoirs distinguished. The supplied shape does not cover every charted part of the entire hydrologic reservoir and is not an accurate shoreline.

map_comparison.method: Full-source-ring visual comparison on the primary chart, aided by approximate main-neatline graticule registration; all 92 source positions drawn for local inspection. No shoreline digitization or repair.
map_comparison.main_map_coverage: 33°10′–34°35′E,48°30′–49°10′N, with enlarged upper-reach and port insets
supported_shape_features: Long northwest-to-southeast reservoir body ending at the Kamianske/Romankove dam sector
Branching embayment in the Vorskla mouth sector
Broad lower body by Verkhnodniprovsk and Kamianske
extent_discrepancies: The source upper cap near 33.54°E/49.00°N omits the charted narrow upper reservoir continuation toward Kremenchuk and its dam.
One generalized outer ring has no island holes, while the chart depicts many islands and channels.
Coarse straight shoreline segments include land and omit local water/tributary-arm details; exact containment and hydrologic completeness are not claimed.
The comparison is approximate and does not establish chart datum equivalence, precise dam-boundary alignment, or today’s waterline.

neighbor_disambiguation.relationship: Upstream of the Kremenchuk dam, separately labelled on the chart; not the source polygon’s principal waterbody
Downstream of the Kamianske end, separately labelled; not the source polygon’s principal waterbody

map_comparison.tributary_scope: Vorskla is directly identified by the chart and chart-set scope. Psel and Oril are separately labelled context; their entire channels or basins do not inherit the reservoir name. No automatic labels are proposed for every embayment.
map_comparison.composite_scope: Single Polygon feature and one complete decoded fragment. The main-waterbody identity is coherent rather than a deliberate multi-reservoir aggregate; generalized margins do not prove exact exclusion of every neighboring water or land patch.
